title: Nebraska: Option Dynasty
description: Go-for-two heartbreak, a fumblerooski trick play, and a split national title—five steps into the 1990s Husker empire.
imageHint: Option pitches and a sea of red in the 1990s

questions.question: Which Nebraska coach won national titles in 1994, 1995, and 1997 after decades as Devaney's offensive assistant?
questions.explanation: Twenty-five seasons as head coach, 255 wins, and a farewell lap into Congress. The argument in Lincoln isn't whether he belongs on the mountain—it's which title year was most Nebraska.

questions.question: In the 1984 Orange Bowl, Osborne's undefeated Huskers trailed Miami late—and he famously went for what instead of a near-certain tying kick?
questions.explanation: Turner Gill's pass failed. Miami won 31–30. Osborne later said he'd make the same call again—championships shouldn't be shared on a kick he didn't need to respect.

questions.question: Before that failed two-point conversion haunted the state, which Husker offensive lineman scored on the "Fumblerooski" in the same Orange Bowl?
questions.explanation: Center snaps, QB "fumbles" the ball to the ground, guard Steinkuhler scoops and runs. It worked for a touchdown. The two-point try later that night still haunts the state.

questions.question: By the mid-90s title years after Steinkuhler's era, Osborne's dominant offensive line earned what nickname?
questions.explanation: Line coach Milt Tenopir lost four starters after 1994, and the 1995 Pipeline still paved 399.8 rushing yards a game. Option football dies without those five.

questions.question: After the Pipeline years, Osborne's 1997 national title was split—Nebraska took the coaches' poll after beating which team in the Orange Bowl?
questions.explanation: Peyton Manning's Vols fell 42–17. Michigan got the AP vote after the Rose Bowl. Nebraska fans still call 1997 a three-peat with footnotes—and they can recite every footnote.

deeperMode.title: Deeper: Option Bloodwork
deeperMode.description: For anyone who still argues 1995 vs 1997 in a bar

questions.question: Which Nebraska quarterback ran the option through the 1994–95 title seasons and the Fiesta Bowl demolition of Florida?
questions.hint: His 75-yard option TD in the '96 Fiesta Bowl is the dynasty's signature clip

questions.question: In that 1996 Fiesta Bowl (1995 season), Nebraska beat Florida by what final score—still a title-game wrecking?
questions.hint: Steve Spurrier's Fun 'n' Gun met the Pipeline at altitude of humiliation

easterEgg.title: He'd go for two again
easterEgg.text: Osborne never apologized for 1984. In interviews years later he still preferred losing by a yard on two to backing into a title with a kick. That stubbornness is the dynasty's origin story.
